transcript.user_1_turn_1: I'm working on the anniversary scrapbook again. I have about thirty photos for the main section, and I'm trying not to make every page look exactly the same.
transcript.user_2_turn_1: Mixing layouts will help. You could use a square photo as the focus on some pages and arrange smaller 4x6 prints around it.
transcript.user_1_turn_2: That sounds better. I'm leaning toward lustre prints too, since people are definitely going to flip through this thing a lot.
transcript.user_2_turn_2: Lustre is a good fit for that. It keeps the color looking lively without showing fingerprints and glare as much as glossy paper.
transcript.user_1_turn_3: Dad wants to look through it with me later. He uses a walker now, and even on pretty normal outings he gets tired quickly if we stay on our feet too long.
transcript.user_2_turn_3: Then keeping things comfortable and unhurried will probably make the afternoon more enjoyable for both of you.
transcript.user_1_turn_4: That's the plan. Before we sit down with the album, I thought we could get outside for a bit because the weather is nice.
transcript.user_2_turn_4: A short walk before the scrapbook sounds like a good change of pace.
transcript.user_1_turn_5: I checked the park map. There's a 600-meter garden loop with benches along the way, and a two-kilometer loop around the lake. The lake one is prettier, but apparently there's nowhere to sit until you're almost back at the entrance.
transcript.user_2_turn_5: The lake route sounds better for scenery, while the garden loop sounds easier if you want something more relaxed.
transcript.user_1_turn_6: We only have an hour or so before dinner anyway, so I'm not trying to turn it into a whole expedition.
transcript.user_2_turn_6: That should be plenty of time for a little fresh air and then the scrapbook.
transcript.user_1_turn_7: Dad says he's ready whenever I am. I saved the lakeside loop on my phone because the water should look really nice this afternoon.
